handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.name: Little Egret
handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.habitat: Habits: Forages slowly along shallow shorelines and mudflats, elegant yet alert; active by day, roosts in trees or reeds at dusk, flies off when startled.
handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.tip: Tip: Ambush riverside shallows while sneaking; alarm distance is about 8 blocks. Use a 200mm+ tele lens from 20m away; focus on the eye and keep shutter at 1/500s or faster to freeze the wingbeat.
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.name: Tree Sparrow
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.habitat: Habits: The most common bird in villages and farmlands; gathers in flocks, hops and pecks on the ground, not very shy of people. Active by day, roosts under eaves or in bushes at night.
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.tip: Tip: Sparrows have a very short alarm distance - a 50mm lens works. Catch them pecking on the ground at 1/250s or faster; sit still by the village entrance and let them come to you.
handbook.birdwatch.tit.name: Great Tit
handbook.birdwatch.tit.habitat: Habits: A lively little bird of forests and woodland edges; hops among canopy branches foraging, sometimes drops to the ground. Active by day with a crisp call.
handbook.birdwatch.tit.tip: Tip: Great Tits never stop hopping in the canopy - use a 200mm+ lens, lock focus and track. Shutter at 1/500s or faster; they are most active at dawn.
